page.layout: Top: a synopsis diagram across the page with braces, reading roughly from "Officium est" on the left to "Temperantia" on the right, under the centred heading "IDEA LIBRI I."; running head centred above the diagram; page number at upper right. Below the diagram, centred: "M. T. CIC. OFFICIORUM / LIBER II." and a Greek line with "expositus." One column of running text in full width, with paragraphs I to VI. Marginal notes in the right margin: "Utile." beside III and "Bona." beside VI.

main_text.head: IDEA LIBRI I.
main_text.l: Simpliciter cujus genera sunt virtutes quatuor Comparatè.
main_text.head: M. T. CIC. OFFICIORUM LIBER II.
ἀφοσιστικῶς[?] expositus.

p.i: I. Nunc deinde de utili seorsim.

main_text.p: II. Idq; tum simpliciter etiam, tum comparatè.
III. Utile autem est, quod honestè pro-Utile.dest.

p.i: IV. Quamvis enim distinctum est genere ipso ab Honesto: tamen nisi honestè fiat, utile non est. Ita enim pars quædam formæ est; sicut sanctè censuit Socrates.
V. Ergo hic quid prosit & quemadmodum honestè prosit, videndum. In his enim consistit forma utilitatis.

main_text.p: VI. Quod prodest & utile dicitur, tumBona. hominem ipsum, tum ejus vitam attin-git.

page.notes: Diagram: box levels and line grouping are read from the braces and may be approximate; the label "quae est" beside the right-hand brace is not transcribed as a separate line. The Greek word on the expositus line ("ἀφοσιστικῶς") is uncertain and marked [?]. The "cō" in "Medium, quod cō siderātur" is printed with an abbreviation mark, copied as seen. Long s is rendered as plain s throughout. Marginal notes "Utile." and "Bona." are placed at their printed lines; their letter marks are absent, as none is printed.
